subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If y = tan⁻¹[(√(1 + x²) + √(1 − x²))/(√(1 + x²) − √(1 − x²))] for 0 < |x| < 1, find dy/dx.

mark_split.label: Reduce the bracket to one tangent
Write y in terms of x

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.205, chapter 9 DIFFERENTIATION, Long Answer question 3. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The split follows the shape this bank uses for a Maths-1B Section C question. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C runs Q19 to Q21 at 8 marks each, answer any 2 of 3, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The mathematics was checked independently before writing, in two parts. First the closed form: the printed expression and π/4 + ½ Cos⁻¹(x²) agreed to nine decimal places at x = 0.3, 0.6, 0.9, −0.5 and −0.8. Then the derivative: −x/√(1 − x⁴) matched a central difference quotient at all five of those values — for example x = 0.6 gives −0.643119694 both ways, and x = −0.8 gives +1.041158413 both ways. Note the sign: y is an even function of x, so dy/dx is negative for positive x and positive for negative x. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A, Maths-2B and Maths-1A expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you substitute, and what the bracket becomes after the substitution.
formula_note: The substitution is x² = cos 2θ, not x = cos 2θ, because x² is what appears under both square roots. A sibling question with a single square root of (1−x)/(1+x) uses the plain x = cos 2θ instead — check whether it is x or x² that matches the expression before substituting.

steps.label: Substitute x² = cos 2θ
steps.margin_note: First two marks. Substituting x² and not x is the choice that makes this short, because both roots contain x² and neither contains x on its own. Write down the range of θ as well — the last two steps depend on it.
lines: The restriction is needed at both ends:
|x| < 1 keeps 1 − x² ≥ 0, and x ≠ 0 is required because
at x = 0 the denominator √(1 + x²) − √(1 − x²) is 0
and the fraction has no value.
(0 < x² < 1 gives an angle 2θ in (0, π/2) with cos 2θ = x²,
0 < |x| < 1 gives 0 < x² < 1, so put x² = cos 2θ.
∴ √(1 + x²) = √2 cos θ   and   √(1 − x²) = √2 sin θ

recall.must_convey: That x² = cos 2θ is substituted, so the two roots become √2 cos θ and √2 sin θ.
accept: put x squared equal to cos two theta
one plus cos two theta is two cos squared theta
the roots become root two cos theta and root two sin theta
x square ni cos two theta ga substitute cheyyali

steps.why: Both roots contain x² and neither contains x by itself, so the substitution is made on x². Setting x² = cos 2θ turns 1 + x² and 1 − x² into perfect squares, so both square roots can be removed.
common_mistakes: Putting x = cos 2θ instead of x² = cos 2θ, which leaves 1 + x² as 1 + cos²2θ and simplifies nothing.
Taking √(2sin²θ) as ±√2 sin θ. The range 0 < θ < π/4 makes sin θ positive, so only the plus sign occurs.
steps.memory_tip: The pair 1 + cos 2θ = 2cos²θ and 1 − cos 2θ = 2sin²θ is what turns a sum and a difference into two squares. Whenever 1 ± something appears under a root, look for it.

steps.label: Reduce the bracket to one tangent
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Dividing the top and the bottom by cos θ is the move that produces tan θ; after that the compound angle form of tan(π/4 + θ) is recognised, not derived.
lines: Substitute both roots into the bracket.

lines.text: (divide the top and the bottom by √2)

lines: so divide the top and the bottom by cos θ:

lines.text: (the formula tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A
tan B), with A = π/4 and B = θ)

recall.must_convey: That dividing by cos θ gives (1 + tan θ)/(1 − tan θ), which is tan(π/4 + θ).
accept: divide the top and the bottom by cos theta
one plus tan theta over one minus tan theta is tan of pi by four plus theta
root two cancels from both parts
cos theta tho divide cheste tan form vasthundi
recognise the compound angle formula for tangent
the whole bracket becomes a single tangent

steps.why: The whole bracket has to become a single tangent before the inverse tangent can be removed. Dividing by cos θ is what produces tan θ, and (1 + tan θ)/(1 − tan θ) is then recognised as the expansion of tan(π/4 + θ) because tan(π/4) = 1.
common_mistakes: Squaring the fraction to clear the roots, which brings back a surd and does not lead to a tangent.
Writing (1 + tan θ)/(1 − tan θ) as tan(π/4 − θ), which is the same expression with the signs swapped.
steps.memory_tip: (1 + tan θ)/(1 − tan θ) is always tan(π/4 + θ), because the 1 in each place is tan(π/4). The minus sign in the denominator belongs to the plus sign in the angle.

so divide the top and the bottom by cos θ:

steps.label: Remove the inverse tangent
steps.margin_note: Two marks: Tan⁻¹(tan A) = A only when A is inside (−π/2, π/2). Show that π/4 + θ is inside it before writing the next line.
lines: which is the principal range of Tan⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That π/4 + θ lies in the principal range of Tan⁻¹, so y = π/4 + θ.
accept: tan inverse of tan gives back the angle here
pi by four plus theta lies between pi by four and pi by two
the angle is inside the principal range so they cancel
principal range lo unnadu kabatti tan inverse tan cancel avuthundi
y equals pi by four plus theta
check the range before cancelling the inverse
heard_as: between pi by four and pi by two

steps.why: Tan⁻¹(tan A) returns A only while A lies in (−π/2, π/2); outside it the answer differs by a multiple of π. Here 0 < θ < π/4 puts π/4 + θ safely inside, so the cancellation is exact and no extra constant appears.
common_mistakes: Cancelling Tan⁻¹ and tan with no check on the range, which is the same working that goes wrong on many other questions of this type.
Reading the range of Tan⁻¹ as [0, π], which belongs to Cos⁻¹.
steps.memory_tip: Remember three principal ranges: Sin⁻¹ gives [−π/2, π/2], Tan⁻¹ gives (−π/2, π/2), Cos⁻¹ gives [0, π]. Cos⁻¹ is the one of the three whose range starts at 0.
lines_compact: which is the principal range of Tan⁻¹.

steps.label: Write y in terms of x
steps.margin_note: One mark. Going back to x before differentiating is shorter than differentiating in θ and then finding dθ/dx separately.

recall.must_convey: That θ = ½ Cos⁻¹(x²), so y = π/4 + ½ Cos⁻¹(x²).
accept: theta is half of cos inverse x squared
y equals pi by four plus half cos inverse x squared
put theta back in terms of x before differentiating
theta ni x lo rasi tarvata differentiate cheyyali
invert the substitution to get theta
return to the original variable

steps.why: The question asks for dy/dx, so y must be written as a function of x before differentiating. Inverting the substitution costs one line, while differentiating in θ needs dθ/dx worked out separately.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as y = π/4 + θ and calling it finished, when the question asks for dy/dx.
Writing θ = Cos⁻¹(x²) and dropping the factor of one half.
steps.memory_tip: The substitution was x² = cos 2θ, so undoing it gives 2θ first and θ second. The one half comes from that 2.

steps.label: Differentiate
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Two things carry it: the minus sign from Cos⁻¹, and the inner derivative 2x. The 2 from 2x cancels the one half, which is why the answer is as clean as it is.

recall.must_convey: That differentiating π/4 + ½ Cos⁻¹(x²) gives −x/√(1 − x⁴).
accept: the derivative of cos inverse carries a minus sign
chain rule brings down two x and it cancels the half
the answer is minus x over root one minus x to the fourth
cos inverse ki minus sign vasthundi, chain rule apply cheyyali
differentiate the cos inverse term and the constant gives zero
minus x by root of one minus x power four
heard_as: root one minus x to the four

steps.why: Cos⁻¹ differentiates with a minus sign while Sin⁻¹ does not, and that single sign is the difference between the right answer and its negative. The inner factor 2x cancels the one half left from θ = ½ Cos⁻¹(x²).
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign from the derivative of Cos⁻¹ and reporting x/√(1 − x⁴).
Writing √(1 − x²) in the denominator instead of √(1 − x⁴), by forgetting that u is x² and not x.
steps.memory_tip: Sin⁻¹ and Cos⁻¹ have the same denominator and opposite signs. Cos⁻¹ takes the minus, because the cosine decreases as the angle grows from 0 to π.

insider_note: Put x² = cos 2θ, not x = cos θ, so both roots simplify together. x ≠ 0 matters because the denominator vanishes there, which is why the range is 0 < |x| < 1.
